{{short description|Ellipsoid most closely containing, or contained in, an n-dimensional convex object}}
[[File:Lowner_Ellipse.webm|thumb|Outer Löwner–John ellipsoid containing a set of a points in {{tmath|\R^2}}]]

In [[mathematics]], the '''John ellipsoid''' or '''Löwner–John ellipsoid''' {{math|''E''(''K'')}} associated to a [[convex body]] {{mvar|K}} in {{mvar|n}}-[[dimension]]al [[Euclidean space]] {{tmath|\R^n}} can refer to the {{mvar|n}}-dimensional [[ellipsoid]] of maximal [[volume]] contained within {{mvar|K}} or the ellipsoid of minimal volume that contains {{mvar|K}}.

Often, the minimal volume ellipsoid is called the [[Charles Loewner|Löwner]] ellipsoid, and the maximal volume ellipsoid is called the John ellipsoid (although John worked with the minimal volume ellipsoid in his original paper).<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Güler|first1=Osman|last2=Gürtuna|first2=Filiz|date=2012|title=Symmetry of convex sets and its applications to the extremal ellipsoids of convex bodies|url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/10556788.2011.626037|journal=Optimization Methods and Software|language=en|volume=27|issue=4–5|pages=735–759|doi=10.1080/10556788.2011.626037|s2cid=2971340 |issn=1055-6788|url-access=subscription}}</ref> One can also refer to the minimal volume circumscribed ellipsoid as the '''outer''' '''Löwner–John ellipsoid''', and the maximum volume inscribed ellipsoid as the '''inner''' '''Löwner–John ellipsoid'''.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Ben-Tal, A.|title=Lectures on modern convex optimization: analysis, algorithms, and engineering applications|date=2001|publisher=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|others=Nemirovskiĭ, Arkadiĭ Semenovich.|isbn=0-89871-491-5|location=Philadelphia, PA|oclc=46538510}}</ref>

The German-American [[mathematician]] [[Fritz John]] proved in 1948 that each convex body in {{tmath|\R^n}} is circumscribed by a unique ellipsoid of minimal volume, and that the dilation of this ellipsoid by factor {{math|1/''n''}} is contained inside the convex body.<ref name="john">John, Fritz. "Extremum problems with inequalities as subsidiary conditions".  ''Studies and Essays Presented to R. Courant on his 60th Birthday'', January 8, 1948,  187—204. Interscience Publishers, Inc., New York, N. Y., 1948. {{oclc|1871554}} {{MR|30135}}</ref> That is, the outer Lowner-John ellipsoid is larger than the inner one by a factor of at most {{mvar|n}}. For a [[Balanced set|balanced]] body, this factor can be reduced to <math>\sqrt{n}.</math>

== Properties ==
The inner Löwner–John ellipsoid {{math|''E''(''K'')}} of a convex body <math>K \subset \R^n</math> is a [[closed unit ball]] {{mvar|B}} in {{tmath|\R^n}} [[if and only if]] {{math|''B'' ⊆ ''K''}} and there exists an [[integer]] {{math|''m'' ≥ ''n''}} and, for {{math|1=''i'' = 1, ..., ''m''}}, [[real number]]s {{math|''c''<sub>''i''</sub> &gt; 0}} and [[unit vector]]s <math>u_i \in S^{n-1} \cap \partial K</math> (where {{mvar|S}} is the unit [[n-sphere]]) such that<ref>{{cite journal|last=Ball|first=Keith M.|year=1992|title=Ellipsoids of maximal volume in convex bodies|journal=Geom. Dedicata|volume=41|issue=2|pages=241&ndash;250|arxiv=math/9201217|doi=10.1007/BF00182424|s2cid=18330466 |issn=0046-5755}}</ref>

<math display=block>\sum_{i = 1}^m c_i u_i = 0</math>

and, for all <math>x \in \R^n:</math>

<math display=block>x = \sum_{i = 1}^m c_i (x \cdot u_i) u_i.</math>

==Computation==
In general, computing the John ellipsoid of a given convex body is a hard problem. However, for some specific cases, explicit formulas are known. Some cases are particularly important for the [[ellipsoid method]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite Geometric Algorithms and Combinatorial Optimization}}</ref>{{Rp|page=|location=|pages=70–73}}

Let {{math|''E''('''A''', '''a''')}} be an ellipsoid in {{tmath|\R^n,}} defined by a matrix {{math|'''A'''}} and center {{math|'''a'''}}. Let {{math|'''c'''}} be a nonzero vector in {{tmath|\R^n.}} Let {{math|''E{{'}}''('''A''', '''a''', '''c''')}} be the half-ellipsoid derived by cutting {{math|''E''('''A''', '''a''')}} at its center using the hyperplane defined by {{math|'''c'''}}. Then, the Lowner-John ellipsoid of {{math|''E{{'}}''('''A''', '''a''', '''c''')}} is an ellipsoid {{math|''E''('''A{{'}}''', '''a{{'}}''')}} defined by:
<math display=block>\begin{align}
  \mathbf{a'} &= \mathbf{a} - \frac{1}{n+1} \mathbf{b} \\
  \mathbf{A'} &= \frac{n^2}{n^2-1} \left(\mathbf{A} - \frac{2}{n+1} \mathbf{bb}^\mathrm{T} \right)
\end{align}</math>
where {{math|'''b'''}} is a vector defined by:
<math display=block>\mathbf{b} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathbf{c}^\mathrm{T} \mathbf{Ac}}} \mathbf{Ac}</math>
Similarly, there are formulas for other sections of ellipsoids, not necessarily through its center.

== Applications ==
The computation of Löwner–John ellipsoids (and in more general, the computation of minimal-volume polynomial level sets enclosing a set) has found many applications in [[Control theory|control]] and [[robotics]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dabbene |first1=Fabrizio |last2=Henrion |first2=Didier |last3=Lagoa |first3=Constantino M. |date=2017 |title=Simple approximations of semialgebraic sets and their applications to control |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0005109816304563 |journal=Automatica |language=en |volume=78 |pages=110–118 |arxiv=1509.04200 |doi=10.1016/j.automatica.2016.11.021|s2cid=5778355 }}</ref> In particular, computing Löwner–John ellipsoids has applications in [[Collision detection|obstacle collision detection]] for robotic systems, where the distance between a robot and its surrounding environment is estimated using a best ellipsoid fit.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Rimon |first1=Elon |last2=Boyd |first2=Stephen |year=1997 |title=Obstacle Collision Detection Using Best Ellipsoid Fit |journal=Journal of Intelligent and Robotic Systems |volume=18 |issue=2 |pages=105–126 |doi=10.1023/A:1007960531949 |s2cid=10505238}}</ref>

Löwner–John ellipsoids has also been used to approximate the optimal policy in [[portfolio optimization]] problems with transaction costs.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Shen|first1=Weiwei|last2=Wang|first2=Jun|title=Transaction Costs-Aware Portfolio Optimization via Fast Lowner-John Ellipsoid Approximation |journal=Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence |year=2015|url=https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/7b31/2141616f092137c12397a47d11d94ddcea78.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170116192444/https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/7b31/2141616f092137c12397a47d11d94ddcea78.pdf|archive-date=2017-01-16|volume=29 |pages=1854–1860|doi=10.1609/aaai.v29i1.9453 |s2cid=14746495 }}</ref>
